column1: # tests/shard-weights.tsv - per-item wall-clock cost, in SECONDS, for weighted
# CI sharding (`tests/run-tests.sh --shard I/N`; see that file's own `--shard`
# header for the full derivation and the LPT algorithm this table feeds).
# Format: one `<kind>:<name><TAB><seconds>` record per line. `<kind>` is
# `suite`, `linter`, or `stage`, matching the prefixes `shard_work` itself
# prints, so a linter and a suite that happen to share a name can never
# collide. Comments are whole-line, first byte `#`.
# An item with NO row here is never dropped: `_shard_weight_of`
# (tests/run-tests.sh) falls back to `SHARD_DEFAULT_WEIGHT_SECONDS` for any
# key this file does not name.
# THESE TWO ROWS ARE THE ONLY REAL, SOURCED NUMBERS IN THIS FILE TODAY.
# Both are cited directly from tests/run-tests.sh's own long-standing comment
# ("tests/suites/scan.sh alone has run for 91 minutes on a hosted runner while
# `color` finishes in under a second"), not fabricated for this table.
suite:scan
suite:color
# REFRESH THIS FILE DELIBERATELY, from real data, never by generating it.
# Run with `SCOURSH_SHARD_RECORD=<path>` set (CI's own "Run the suite" step
# does this and uploads the result as a `shard-timing-<os>-shard<N>`
# artifact) to collect real `<kind>:<name><TAB><seconds>` lines, then fold
# them into this file by hand. There is deliberately no importer that writes
# this file unattended - a suite's true cost moves with the runner and the
# fixture tree, and an unreviewed auto-update could drift the shard plan
# without anyone deciding it should.
